utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is case IT-98-32-I. The Prosecutor against Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanne Korner. I represent the Prosecution, with the assistance of co-counsel, Ms. Nancy Paterson, and case manager Diane Boles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For the accused? Are you appearing for the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am Slavisa Prodanovic. I am legal counsel today for the accused Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to discuss this matter with your client yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I did have an opportunity of discussing it with my client yesterday and today, and he is aware of the procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And is he aware of the nature of the allegations made against him?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, he is aware, and he is also aware of the plea he is supposed to enter. And we wish to suggest to the Court not to have the factual part of the indictment read, only to have the accused enter his pleas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I am grateful to hear that. But he is ready to enter a plea today, is he?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we actually take the pleas, I should ask the accused: Are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you understand? Are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What is your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And what is the date upon which you believe you were born?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: The 25th of August, 1954.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And what is the address at which you resided before you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Vojvode Stepe 140, Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And you are now ready to enter pleas to the charges against you in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I propose to read out to you just the charge, and then I will ask you: How do you plead to that charge, guilty or not guilty? Your answer in each case should be "guilty" or "not guilty," as the case may be. The first count against you is a charge of extermination, being a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The second count is a charge of persecution on political, racial and religious grounds, as a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The third count is a charge of murder, being a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The fourth count is another charge of murder, as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The fifth count is a charge of inhumane acts, being a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The sixth count is a charge of violence to life and person, being a violation of the laws or customs of war. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The seventh count is a charge of murder, being a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The eighth count is another charge of murder, being a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The ninth count is a charge of inhumane acts, being a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The tenth count is a charge of violence to life and person, being a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The eleventh count is a charge of murder, being a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The twelfth count, a charge of murder, being a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The thirteenth count is a charge of inhumane acts, being a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And the fourteenth and final count is a charge of violence to life and person, being a violation of the laws and customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please, sir. The Registrar will be instructed to fix a date for trial, when appropriate. And the accused is remanded in custody until further order. Is there any matter which the Prosecution wishes to raise at this stage, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to say this: We are in a position to make immediate disclosure of the Rule 47 supporting material, both in English and in B/C/S. But, as I understand the matter, Defence counsel will not be instructed or may not be instructed by his client, and so it may well be that for the moment we'd better, as it were, hang onto it. Can I just mention one other matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we filed a motion for protective measures. We were unaware, at the time that we filed the motion, that Your Honour had issued a scheduling order in respect of another matter, of which Your Honour is seized, effectively asking for clarification of the order that was dealt with in that case. So we will re-examine the motion that we filed, in the light of the order that Your Honour has made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I am grateful to that. There is another matter which you should consider, and that is the definition of the public includes various persons other than the Judges of the Tribunal and the staff of the Registry. Now, that may be interpreted as a term of art, which means those people who work in the Registry, rather than the staff of the Registrar, who also work in Chambers. So at the moment you are denying us the opportunity of showing our own legal officers and secretaries the material that we have to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am very grateful for that. We will reconsider that matter as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. This is a new form, this one, so far as I am aware, and it does need a little bit of cleaning up, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll make sure that the appropriate steps are taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prodanovic, do you want to raise any matter at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: I have nothing special to add, Your Honour. It is true that I shall no longer appear as Defence counsel in this case, because I am busy with another case. However, the accused is quickly going to find a new attorney and all communication will go through him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I am grateful to you for telling us this. You might enforce this with your client, however, that the sooner he does obtain Defence counsel, the sooner he will find out what this is all about, by the material which the Prosecution will provide. It is necessary, of course, to notify the Registry, or the Defence counsel unit anyway, so that the Prosecution are aware of to whom the material should be sent. So will you make sure, before you leave the case, that you explain to your client, your current client, the importance of moving quickly. Well, that's all. We'll adjourn. --- Hearing adjourned at 10.50 a.m. sine die
